take: Record shipping costs are now forcing oil producers to slash prices as delivered crude exceeds what refiners will pay, a clear signal that freight is repricing the crude curve rather than merely following it. The Hormuz crisis has extended beyond crude and gas into the bunker tank, tightening fuel supply for container shipping whilst UK ports push back on Brussels over ETS diversion claims, both of which point to higher effective voyage costs and wider product arbitrage. Fujairah bunker sales have recovered from June's record low but remain more than half below last year, a demand signal that sits awkwardly against firm outright prices and argues for caution on gasoil cracks. The cross-market link is the bunker complex itself: Hormuz disruption to shipping fuel and the AMS methanol-capable newbuild both feed the gasoil-VLSFO spread, whilst West Africa's ore boom absorbing another 120 capesizes by 2030 underpins the tonne-mile story. Watch Hormuz headlines and any Washington escalation against Iran, plus the next Fujairah bunker sales print for confirmation that the demand recovery is real rather than a dead-cat bounce.
